claim: Footnote 24: “It is possible for a conditional adjunct to have scope over a multiple situation, as in She cycled to work if I remember correctly. The adjunct here, however, belongs to the modal category discussed in §18.”
evidence_summary: §18 (p. 773) is “Speech act-related adjuncts”; modal adjuncts are §16 (p. 767). In §16, p. 771 says “conditional adjuncts too can function in this way”, with [14iia] If I’m not mistaken, that’s a kookaburra over there, and p. 666 [2ib] labels He’s going to buy the house if I’m not mistaken “[modal conditional]”. §18’s conditional if you remember/recall (p. 774) “gives the utterance the force of a reminder”.
finding: Change §18 to §16. The category word and the section number disagree; if I remember correctly hedges the speaker’s certainty like if I’m not mistaken, so §16 is the likelier target. Three readers found this independently.
proposed_wording: belongs to the modal category discussed in §16
inference: Does footnote 24 point to the section on modal adjuncts?

evidence.passage: §14.1.1, p. 743 n. 24. “belongs to the modal category discussed in §18”
